purpose: Per-card assertions re-derived from the tree, kept apart from the registry so that editing the registry cannot also edit what the registry is judged against. tools/check_vf_cl_registry.py refuses to run without this file, refuses a card it does not cover, and refuses a closed blocker it carries no checks for -- deleting an entry is a failure, not a silence.
note: impliesImplemented states what the tree shows. When every check under a card holds, the registry's implemented field must equal it: that is what catches a card being reverted to an earlier, internally consistent, but no longer true state. A null means no assertion is made, and why says so out loud rather than leaving a gap that reads as coverage. forbiddenBlockers lists the blocker ids a correction retired; any of them open again is drift. They live here rather than in the registry because a file that can edit the list of things it may not say has not been stopped from saying them.

VF-CL-01.whyCiVerified: The lane that collects this card's tests runs a whole directory (pytest tests/core, pytest tests/), so no check over the tree can say that *this* card's behaviour was exercised rather than its neighbours'. A check pointing at that lane would read as coverage while asserting nothing, so nothing is asserted here. The field stays what the owner recorded, and rule 7 does not confirm it.

VF-CL-04.whyCiVerified: The workflow and checker now support a GitHub/Sigstore-attested CI-produced receipt, but this source tree intentionally carries no authoritative bundle yet. An implementation-only commit cannot attest its later Evidence commit or landing SHA, so rule 7 stays false until an exact-head workflow_dispatch run is verified and its receipt plus bundle are recorded. The path-absent check makes that distinction mechanical: adding the bundle breaks this false derivation and requires a cryptographically verified true claim rather than a prose flip.

VF-CL-05.whyCiVerified: A review card ships review documents. There is no code for CI to execute, which the registry's notApplicable already says; re-deriving it from the tree would mean asserting something about the absence of code, and that is not what these checks can see.
VF-CL-05.why: A review card ships review documents. Their existence in the tree does not re-derive that the reviews were performed, and a check that looked only for file names would read as coverage while asserting nothing. So this card's implemented field is not re-derived here, and that is stated rather than left as an empty entry.
